assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies, followed by the first source associations (the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane), opened neutrino astronomy as an observational window. The instrumental achievement, a cubic-kilometre detector built in Antarctic ice, is original and technically daunting, and it answers a decades-old cosmic-ray-origin question from an experimentalist's viewpoint.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the cubic-kilometre IceCube concept; Karle was central to the detector's construction and optical-sensor/ice calibration; Spiering is credited for early neutrino-telescope development (Baikal, AMANDA lineage). From the supplied credit the three-person configuration is plausible, though a large collaboration and predecessor efforts mean the allocation is not trivially clean. My own knowledge of the exact individual roles is not independently verified.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed in multiple channels and independently supported by other detectors at lower significance. The Galactic-plane result is recent, and the source picture (blazars versus other classes) is still developing, but the core discovery is stable. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Individual roles within the large IceCube collaboration and the AMANDA/Baikal predecessors may be hard to apportion.
Source identification remains incomplete, so the astrophysical interpretation may keep evolving.
The credited names may omit other decisive contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental observation of the Higgs boson in 2012 closed the Standard Model's particle content and verified the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism proposed in the 1960s. It rests on two enormous, independent experiments, the instrument-building and analysis at the highest level, and its importance is beyond dispute.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize went to the theorists. The experimental recognition must go to individuals while honouring two collaborations: Jenni (ATLAS founding spokesperson), Virdee (CMS founding figure) and Gianotti (ATLAS spokesperson at the time of discovery) give a balanced ATLAS/CMS split. Della Negra is also a founding CMS leader and the three-name limit forces a hard exclusion. Any choice carries credit-allocation controversy.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by two experiments and by all subsequent LHC data; couplings measured steadily. Recognition of the experiment is arguably overdue relative to the theory prize, but the institutional-credit problem has delayed it.
uncertainties: Selecting three of four credited names excludes Michel Della Negra, who may be equally deserving.
Prize rules versus the collaborative nature of the discovery; some members may feel the 2013 prize already covers it.
Whether the credit should centre on founders or on those leading the discovery year is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2011 Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum-model prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle, followed by the 2018 observations of correlated-insulator and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, created the field of twistronics and tunable correlated moire matter. This is a rare theory-to-experiment narrative with large downstream impact on condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero led the experimental discovery of the correlated and superconducting states. The supplied triad is a natural prize configuration. The first author of the 2018 experimental papers (Yuan Cao) is not in the credited names, which I note as a graduate-student-level credit gap rather than a barrier.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups worldwide within a few years, with a rich follow-up (fractional Chern insulators, etc.). The field is still young and the nature of the superconductivity is debated, so recognition could be somewhat early, but the confirmation is broad.
uncertainties: Nature of the superconducting pairing remains disputed.
Possible premature recognition while the field is still rapidly evolving.
Other early moire-band theory contributors (e.g. Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Morell et al.) may deserve consideration; I cannot verify the priority claims independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered precise full-sky CMB temperature and polarization maps, fixing the cosmological parameters to percent level and establishing the Lambda-CDM concordance model, including early-universe constraints on reionization and inflation-consistent initial conditions. As an instrument and measurement it is exemplary precision astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the WMAP mission as principal investigator, Spergel was the leading analyst and theory interpreter, and Page was a key instrument and design scientist. A three-person prize is plausible. The 2006 prize to Mather and Smoot (COBE) and the 2019 prize to Peebles overlap with the field, which affects how the committee views a second CMB recognition.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed and superseded in precision by Planck, with a stable interpretation. Recognition would be timely or somewhat late; open questions such as the Hubble tension do not undermine the WMAP measurement.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier CMB prizes may reduce appetite for another CMB award.
Planck's later precision may lead some to prefer a broader or alternative formulation.
Attribution within a large team is not unique.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2019 first image of the M87 supermassive black hole's shadow, and the 2022 Sgr A* image, provided direct horizon-scale evidence consistent with general relativity and showed Earth-sized very-long-baseline interferometry at 1.3 mm. This is a landmark experiment with major public and scientific impact.
assessment.attribution: Doeleman led the EHT collaboration and the VLBI technology development; Falcke proposed the shadow-imaging concept and contributed to the project's scientific case; Narayan contributed the accretion-flow theory underpinning the interpretation. The supplied triad covers instrumentation, concept, and theory, though the 2020 prize for black holes (Penrose, Genzel, Ghez) and the large collaboration complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Two independent targets imaged and consistent over several epochs; polarization results add confirmation. The interpretation is stable, though the data come from one collaboration with essentially one array, so independent replication is limited.
uncertainties: Independence of confirmation is limited since all images come from the same collaboration.
Large-collaboration credit and the exclusion of many essential instrument builders.
Overlap with the 2020 black-hole prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED translated cavity-QED ideas to superconducting circuits, enabling strong coupling, dispersive readout and the architecture of modern superconducting quantum processors. The platform underlies the leading qubit technology and the foundational experiments in quantum measurement.
assessment.attribution: Blais provided the 2004 theoretical proposal with collaborators; Wallraff and Schoelkopf with colleagues produced the 2004 experimental demonstration and subsequent development. The theory/experiment split is clean among the supplied names, though co-authors on the foundational papers, such as Girvin, are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and now industrial. The 2025 prize (macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits) recognised neighbouring superconducting-circuit work, so a second prize in the same family could be viewed as premature or duplicative.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize for superconducting circuits.
Credit for foundational papers beyond the three credited names is not fully resolved.
Whether the core discovery is the physics or the engineering platform.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip detectors and hybrid pixel detectors transformed vertex and tracking systems in particle physics, enabling heavy-flavour tagging and the precision tracking used in LHC experiments, including the Higgs discovery. From my own background in detector instrumentation I regard this as a high-impact, enabling invention that the prize has treated favourably in the past (Charpak 1992).
assessment.attribution: Parker developed microstrip detectors with collaborators; Heijne and Jarron are credited for the hybrid-pixel concept at CERN. The invention was incremental and collaborative, with others such as Kemmer (planar process) and Rossi/Heijne groups contributing. I cannot verify the priority claims independently.
assessment.maturity: Mature, decades of use, and independently validated. Recognition would be late but fully supported by impact.
uncertainties: Contributions are distributed among many individuals and groups, so a clean three-person credit is doubtful.
Instrumentation prizes rely on the committee judging an invention rather than a discovery.
Priority claims, notably Kemmer and others on planar silicon detectors, are not covered in the supplied credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84) and entanglement-based cryptography established that secrecy can be grounded in quantum mechanics, and sparked quantum information science. Experiments have realized it over fibre and satellite links, which ties it to physical measurement, though the core contribution is conceptual.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84, the decisive protocol. Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is a distinct contribution, and the third slot is a genuine allocation question. I propose two names to keep the credit clean; this leaves Ekert's role unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Over four decades old, experimentally implemented, and commercially relevant. The 2022 prize covered Bell-inequality experiments, so recognition is arguably timely for the theory side.
uncertainties: Ekert's role versus BB84 priority is unresolved.
Practical security issues (side channels) are not central to the principle but affect assessment of impact.
Overlap with the 2022 prize and the broader quantum-information list.
